::: {#rem-subset-template}
#### The shape of a subset proof

By @def-subset, $A \subseteq B$ means the conditional
"if $a \in A$, then $a \in B$" is true for every $a$.
So a proof of $A \subseteq B$ is a proof of that conditional,
either directly (@def-direct-proof):

> | Suppose $a \in A$.
> | $\vdots$
> | Therefore $a \in B$.
> | So $A \subseteq B$.

or by contrapositive (@def-proof-by-contrapositive):

> | Suppose $a \notin B$.
> | $\vdots$
> | Therefore $a \notin A$.
> | So $A \subseteq B$.

The element $a$ is arbitrary: the proof may use only that $a \in A$ (or that $a \notin B$),
nothing else about it.

:::
